title: Product PRD: Unified Inference - Overview, Requirements, Roadmap & Pricing (2026-11-20)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, requirements, architecture/design notes, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product series (hosted, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product managers, engineering leads, go-to-market, and customer success teams.

Goals
- Provide a single source of truth for product scope and launch plan for Unified Inference vNext.
- Align engineering, SRE, sales, and support on SLOs, rollout sequence, pricing, and post-release observability.
- Document non-functional requirements that drive architecture and prioritization (latency, cost targets, reliability).

1) Product overview

What: Unified Inference is Redwood's consolidated product offering that standardizes the inference API and operational tooling across Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The goal is to simplify developer experience while giving platform teams predictable economics and enterprise controls.

Key capabilities (customer-facing):
- Text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking via a single REST/SDK surface.
- Streaming responses, function-calling, and structured outputs.
- Smart routing policies (latency, cost, region, tier) with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations through Redwood Optimize integration.
- Observability: per-model/route token cost, latency breakdowns, and quality regressions tied to evals.

Target customers:
- AI-native startups and product teams needing low-friction hosted APIs.
- Platform teams requiring reserved capacity and predictable throughput.
- Regulated customers needing Private deployments, KMS integrations, and audit logging.

2) PRD summary and high-level requirements

Primary objectives:
1. Deliver a single API and config surface that behaves consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
2. Meet predictable unit economics: per-token cost and tail latency targets for common scenarios.
3. Provide rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and first-class observability for regressions.

User stories (representative):
- As an app engineer, I want to switch between hosted and dedicated model endpoints without changing client code so I can scale reliably.
- As a platform owner, I want SLA-backed latency and throughput guarantees for reserved capacity to support peak business traffic.
- As a security officer, I want Private deployments to support KMS integration and audit logs for compliance.

Functional requirements (MUST):
- Common API: identical REST and SDK semantics for text/chat/embeddings across deployment modes.
- Model version pinning and rollout policies: per-route version pin, canary rollout with configurable traffic percentage and auto-rollback on error thresholds.
- Smart routing engine: routing rules by latency SLA, cost budget, region, and customer tier.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, model-quality regressions (linked to evals).
- Failure modes: transparent fallback to pre-configured alternate model variants with preserved schema.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- Latency targets: 95th-percentile < 300ms for short-generation requests (<= 64 tokens) on Hosted in region for curated models.
- Cost targets: reduce per-token cost by 20% vs baseline using batching/caching/quantization recommendations for eligible workloads.
- Throughput: Dedicated pools should sustain 5k concurrent streaming requests per 1K-GPU pool (configurable).
- Security: support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and audit logs retention configurable to 365 days.

3) Design and architecture notes

Runtime and orchestration (high-level):
- Serving runtime: unified inference engine with kernel selection, dynamic batching, and KV cache management.
- Smart routing service: policy engine consults capacity, latency SLO, and cost profiles to route request.
- Control plane: model catalog, rollout policies, billing attribution, and observability exporters.
- Data plane: runtime pods/instances for Hosted and Dedicated; customer-managed agents for Private.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Batching vs latency: dynamic batching with latency SLO-preserving thresholds; fallback to immediate dispatch when latency budget exhausted.
- Quantization compatibility: ensure model variants are marked as compatible in model catalog; runtime must enforce mismatch checks and fallback.
- Cache consistency: prefix/KV cache invalidation on model or prompt-template updates.

Ownership and signal owners:
- Product: Aisha Patel (PM) \u2014 overall product requirements and roadmap prioritization.
- Eng - Serving Runtime: Priya Desai \u2014 kernel selection, batching, KV cache.
- Eng - Platform: Tom Nguyen \u2014 control plane rollouts, catalog, routing.
- Eng - SRE: Samir Rao \u2014 SLO definitions, alerting thresholds, capacity planning.
- GTM: Elena Garcia \u2014 pricing, packaging, sales enablement.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)

Themes and milestones:
- Q2 2026: Core API alignment + model-catalog consolidation.
- Q3 2026: Smart routing MVP and Dedicated capacity autoscaling.
- Q4 2026: Private deployment GA (VPC + on-prem installable package) + KMS integrations.
- Q1 2027: Redwood Optimize integration v2 (automated quantization suggestions + cost-aware batching).
- Q2 2027: Quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval sets; developer-facing rollouts UI.

Quarterly milestones (selected):
1. 2026-06: API parity across Hosted/Dedicated (text/chat/embeddings).
2. 2026-09: Smart routing 1.0 (latency/cost-based policy; basic fallback).
3. 2026-12: Private GA + enterprise compliance checklist.
4. 2027-03: Optimize automatic recommendations (batching/quantization).

Rollout sequence and gating criteria:
- Internal beta with four strategic customers (Dedicated & Private) -> 30-day production soak -> broader GA.
- Gating KPIs: p95 latency within 120% of target, <1% rollback incidents, no data-plane security findings in external audit.

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing tiers (high-level):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing with tiered discounts at usage thresholds. Base: $0.0008 per input token / $0.0020 per output token for standard curated models (example).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitment with guaranteed throughput and per-token micro-billing for overages. Starter: 4-GPU pool reserved at $X/month (configurable); committed usage discounts 25-40% vs Hosted list price.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + deployment fee + optional support & compliance add-ons. Includes KMS/HSM integration and audit logging.

Packaging notes and upsell motions:
- Offer \u201cmigration credits\u201d (1-3 months) for customers shifting from Hosted to Dedicated to offset onboarding risk.
- Upsell Redwood Optimize add-on for teams focused on cost-per-token reductions; pricing as percentage of cost savings (typical 10-20%).
- Professional services: onboarding, performance tuning, custom quantization/profile work.

Pricing guardrails and tracking metrics:
- Unit economics tracked per-model per-customer (tokens in/out, GPU-hours, cache hit rate, batching efficiency).
- GTM to monitor CAC payback and migration conversion rates from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

6) Release notes (most recent major release: 2026-11-20)

Release: Unified Inference v2026-11.20 (GA)
Highlights:
- Private deployment GA: VPC installer, KMS integration, 365-day audit logs retention.
- Smart routing beta: latency and cost policy rules + automatic fallback to compatible variants.
- API parity achieved for text/chat/embeddings across Hosted and Dedicated.
- Observability: added per-route token-cost breakdown and p99 latency tracing.

Operational notes for support and SRE:
- SLOs:
  - Hosted: p95 latency <= 300ms for short requests; error rate <= 0.5%; availability >= 99.9% per region.
  - Dedicated: target p99 latency <= 1s under committed throughput; availability SLA 99.95%.
- Alerts and runbooks:
  - Token-cost spike alert: threshold = +50% baseline token cost in 15 minutes -> notify billing and SRE.
  - Model-quality regression alert: >10% drop in eval pass rate for critical prompt set -> oncall + model-owner.
  - Fallback cascade: if primary model fails >3% errors for 5 minutes, control plane will shift 50% traffic to fallback model and open an incident.

Known issues and mitigations:
- Large-batch memory regression on 80-token sequences observed on GPU type g4x in Dedicated pools. Mitigation: temporary cap batch_size=16 for g4x; longer-term fix prioritized in runtime team.
- Private installer: TLS handshake failures on specific OpenSSL versions; mitigated with compatibility matrix and cert rotation guidance.

7) Open risks and action items

Open risks:
- Model-variant compatibility matrix gaps could cause rollout failures if not fully populated. (Owner: Platform)
- Cost model accuracy for Private deployments needs refinement (owner: Finance + Product).

Action items (short-term):
1. Platform to complete model-compatibility audit by 2026-12-01. (Owner: Tom Nguyen)
2. Finance to publish Dedicated pricing bands and migration credits structure by 2026-12-10. (Owner: Elena Garcia)
3. Runtime to deliver g4x memory regression patch in 2-week sprint. (Owner: Priya Desai)
